record.title: Farey-interval shape conjecture for Mullineux wall-crossing of the sign representation
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a prime number, let $\operatorname{sgn}_n$ be the partition of $n$ corresponding to the sign representation of $S_n$, and let $r$ be a term in the $n$-th Farey sequence. For $s=p/q$, let $M_s$ be the $q$-Mullineux involution on partitions of $n$, let $0<w_1<\dots<w_k<r$ be the terms of the $n$-th Farey sequence between $0$ and $r$, and define

$$
N_r=M_r\circ M_{w_k}\circ\dots\circ M_{w_1}.
$$

For positive integers $f_1<\dots<f_m$ and $g_1,\dots,g_m$, write $f_1^{g_1}\dots f_m^{g_m}$ for the partition having $g_i$ parts equal to $f_i$. **Farey-interval shape conjecture.** There is an increasing sequence of fractions $a_i/b_i$ in the Farey series such that, whenever $a_i/b_i<r<a_{i+1}/b_{i+1}$, the partition $N_r(\operatorname{sgn}_n)$ has the form $z^t x^y$, where

$$
z+y=b_i
$$

and

$$
y+t+z-x=b_{i+1}.
$$

Together with $xy+zt=n$, these equations constrain the shape of the wall-crossed sign representation. The source presents this as a computer-motivated conjecture and gives no resolution.

record.references:

record.title: The complete-intersection conjecture for uniform partition systems
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}^n_k$ be the family of uniform $k$-partitions of an $n$-set, and let a partition system be **$t$-intersecting** when every two partitions have at least $t$ common classes. For $0\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{k-t}{2}\right\rfloor$, define 
$$
\mathcal{P}_i(n,k,t)=\left\{P\in\mathcal{U}^n_k:\left|P\cap\{[1,c],[c+1,2c],\ldots,[(t+2i-1)c+1,(t+2i)c]\}\right|\geq t+i\right\}.
$$
 

**Complete-intersection conjecture.** For $n\geq k\geq t\geq1$, if $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{U}^n_k$ is $t$-intersecting, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq\max_{0\leq i\leq (k-t)/2}|\mathcal{P}_i(n,k,t)|.
$$
 

The source presents this as the partition-system analogue of the Ahlswede–Khachatrian theorem. It also conjectures uniqueness up to permutations of the ground set; the fuller candidate statement is recorded here as the principal claim.

record.title: Grove formula conjecture for the bounded cube recurrence
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a section, let $f$ be a state, and let $(x_0,y_0,t_0)$ be a point in $\overset{\circ}{Y}\cap\mathcal{L}$ in the future of $S$. Assume that the cone $\mathcal{C}$ meets $S$ in at least one point, and let $W$ be the closure of the prescribed intersection of $S$ with the interior of $\mathcal{C}$ together with the two specified points. A grove is a grove on $W$, and $\mu(G)$ denotes its associated weight. **Grove formula conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that the bounded cube recurrence is computed from $f|_S$ by a formula of the form

$$
f(x_0,y_0,t_0)=c\cdot\sum_{G\in\text{groves on }W}\mu(G).
$$

The formula is intended to express the output of the bounded cube recurrence in terms of the initial state on the section; the source refers to Carroll and Speyer for the definition of groves. The parser supplies no evidence resolving this claim, so its status remains open.

record.title: The regular fine mixed subdivision conjecture for the matroid \(\mathcal{T}_{n,d}\)
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_{n,d}$ be the matroid introduced from the combinatorial encoding of arrangements of $d$ generic complete flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $n\Delta_{d-1}$ be the Minkowski sum of $n$ copies of the simplex $\Delta_{d-1}$, and let a fine mixed subdivision be regular if it is induced by assigning heights to the vertices of the summands and projecting the lower facets of the resulting lifted Minkowski sum. For a basis $B$ of $\mathcal{T}_{n,d}$, say that the simplices of a subdivision are located at $B$ when their locations are exactly the elements of $B$. **The regular fine mixed subdivision conjecture.** For any basis $B$ of $\mathcal{T}_{n,d}$, there is a regular fine mixed subdivision of $n\Delta_{d-1}$ whose $n$ simplices are located at $B$. This is stated as a stronger converse to the preceding conjectural characterization, requiring every matroid basis to arise from a regular fine mixed subdivision; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Realization conjecture for the planar binary tree Hopf algebra
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $(e_\sigma)_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n}$ be a basis of $A_n$, and let $\mathbf P_T$ denote the polynomial associated with a planar binary tree $T$ of size $n$. Let $\rho_{m,n}$ be the morphism associated with the tower, let $\mathcal K=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}K_0(A_n)$, and define the induction product by

$$
[M]\cdot[N]=[M\otimes_{\mathbb C}N\mathord\uparrow_{A_m\otimes A_n}^{A_{m+n}}].
$$

**Realization conjecture.** There exists a tower of algebras $A_n$, with a basis $(e_\sigma)_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n}$, such that the restriction of $\rho_{m,n}$ to canonical words is given by the product of the corresponding $\mathbf P_T$ functions; the indecomposable projective modules of $A_n$ are the left ideals $P_T=A_ne_{\sigma_T}$ and are therefore in bijection with planar binary trees of size $n$; and the map

$$
\mathcal K\longrightarrow\mathbf{PBT}
$$

sending the class of $P_T$ to $\mathbf P_T$ is a ring isomorphism. This conjecture would provide an algebraic realization of the planar binary tree Hopf algebra, refining the existence conjecture and identifying its projective representation theory with the basis of planar binary trees. The source provides no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Adjacency and diameter conjecture for the ridge graph of the quasi-semimetric cone
record.statement:
Let $QMET_n$ be the cone of quasi-semimetrics, with triangle facets, non-negativity facets $NN_{ij}$, and ridge graph $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ whose nodes are the facets of $QMET_n$ and whose edges join adjacent facets. Two vectors are **conflicting** if they have components with nonzero values of different signs.

**Adjacency and diameter conjecture.** (i) A triangle facet is adjacent to a facet if and only if they are non-conflicting. (ii) The non-negativity facets $NN_{ij}$ and $NN_{i'j'}$ are adjacent if and only if neither $i'=j$ nor $j'=i$. (iii) The diameter of $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ is $2$. (iv) The ridge graph $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ is an induced subgraph of $G^{*}_{OMCUT_n}$.

These assertions were checked by computer for $n\leq 7$. The diameter assertion follows formally from the proposed adjacency criteria together with the preceding non-adjacency results, but the general adjacency and induced-subgraph claims remain open.

record.title: Facet classification conjecture for the oriented-multicut cone
record.statement:
Let $OMCUT_n$ be the cone of oriented multicuts. A **zero-extension** of an inequality on $OMCUT_{n-1}$ is the inequality obtained by adding a zero coordinate for the new element. Let $H(b)$ denote a hypermetric inequality, and let $A_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ and $B_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ be the inequalities defined in the paper.

**Oriented-multicut facet conjecture.** The following inequalities define facets of $OMCUT_n$: (i) zero-extensions of every facet of $OMCUT_{n-1}$, including oriented triangle and non-negativity inequalities; (ii) every hypermetric inequality $H(b)$ except non-oriented triangle inequalities; and (iii) the inequalities $A_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ and $B_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$.

The conjecture was checked by computer for $n\leq 7$. Its completeness as a facet description in general remains open.

record.title: The maximum-degree bound for the configuration-wise minimum-light-number gap
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $V(G)$ be its vertex set, let $\deg_G(v)$ denote the degree of a vertex $v$, and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^{V(G)}$ be a configuration. Let $ML_G(x)$ and $ML^*_G(x)$ denote the minimum light numbers of $x$ for the sigma-game and lit-only sigma-game on $G$, respectively.

**Maximum-degree gap conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every configuration $x$,

$$
ML^*_G(x)-ML_G(x)\leq\max_{v\in V(G)}\deg_G(v).
$$

The conjecture is suggested by bounds proved in the paper for graphs obtained from trees by adding loops, unicyclic graphs, and grid graphs. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

record.title: Existence of difficult subgraph-counting identities
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices. For a graph $J$, write $s(J,G)$ for the number of induced subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $J$; let $G_v^-$ and $G_v^+$ denote the subgraphs induced by the vertices not adjacent and adjacent to $v$, respectively. A subgraph-counting identity has the form

$$
\sum_{v\in V(G)} \sum_{a=1}^N m_a(n) \prod_{i=1}^k s(J_{a,i},G^-_v) \prod_{j=1}^l s(J'_{a,j},G^+_v)=0.
$$

Here $m_a(n)$ are polynomials in $n$, and the complexity condition is

$$
\deg m_a(n)+\sum_{i=1}^k |V(J_{a,i})|+\sum_{j=1}^l |V(J'_{a,j})|\leq K
$$

for every $a$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every $K\geq 4$, there is such an identity that holds for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, has one graph $J_{a,i}$ or $J'_{a,j}$ with $K$ vertices, and is not in one of the easily described families.

The paper's proved identity supplies the first example outside the previously known easily described families. The conjecture proposes that difficult identities continue to exist at every complexity level $K\geq4$.

record.title: Conjecture that complete graphs are strongly GT
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, possibly with loops in $H$. Write $\hom(G,H)$ for the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $H$. A graph $H$ is **strongly GT** if, for every graph $G$,

$$
\hom(G\sqcup G,H)\leq \hom(G\times K_2,H).
$$

**Strongly GT conjecture for complete graphs.** For $q\geq 3$, the complete graph $K_q$ is strongly GT.

For $H=K_q$, this would imply the desired upper bound on the number of proper $q$-colorings of an $N$-vertex, $d$-regular graph. The source explains that $K_q$ is not a bipartite swapping target because it contains an induced triangle, but conjectures that it is nevertheless strongly GT. The resolution status is not specified.

record.title: The surface \ce 3-system list-colouring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a fixed surface. For a graph $G$ embeddable on $S$ with a $\Sigma$-system, define

$$
k(G;\Sigma)=\max_{u\ne v}|\Sigma(u)\cap\Sigma(v)|
$$

 and let $\Delta(G;\Sigma)=\max_{v}|\Sigma(v)|$. **The surface $\Sigma$-system list-colouring conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_S$ such that, for every graph $G$ embeddable on $S$,

$$
\mathit{ch}(G;\Sigma)\le\Delta(G;\Sigma)+k(G;\Sigma)+c_S.
$$

This aims to combine the paper's main theorem with a degeneracy-based list-colouring bound, extending the latter to surface-embeddable graphs. The source gives no resolution.

record.title: The semiprimitivity characterization of graph-restrictive permutation groups
record.statement: Let $L$ be a transitive permutation group. It is **semiprimitive** if each of its normal subgroups is either transitive or semiregular, and it is graph-restrictive if there exists a constant $c(L)$ such that, for every connected locally-$L$ pair $(\Gamma,G)$ and every arc $(u,v)$ of $\Gamma$, one has $|G_{uv}|\leq c(L)$. **Semiprimitivity characterization conjecture.** A permutation group is graph-restrictive if and only if it is semiprimitive. The conjecture seeks a characterization of graph-restrictive groups and, in the source, is motivated by results extending methods for primitive groups to semiprimitive groups; its resolution is not stated there.

record.title: The finite-field matching conjecture for equal-sum collisions
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $k\leq p$, and let $a_1,\dots,a_k\in\mathbb F_p$ and $b_1,\dots,b_k\in\mathbb F_p$ be arbitrary elements. **Finite-field matching conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi$ of the indices $1,2,\dots,k$ such that whenever

$$
a_i+b_{\pi(i)}=a_j+b_{\pi(j)},
$$

one has $a_i=a_j$ and $b_{\pi(i)}=b_{\pi(j)}$. This is the finite-field formulation used in the paper's inductive strategy for Snevily's conjecture; the source does not report a resolution.

record.title: Protasov's conjecture on spectrum-maximizing and spectrum-minimizing products
record.statement:
Let $r$ be an odd integer, and let $A_1,A_2$ be the $(r-1)\times(r-1)$ matrices defined by

$$
(A_s)_{ij}=1\quad\text{if }2-s\leq 2j-i\leq r-s+1,
$$

and $(A_s)_{ij}=0$ otherwise, for $s=1,2$. A product is an s.m.p. if it is a spectrum-maximizing product, and an s.l.p. if it is a spectrum-minimizing product. **Protasov's conjecture.** For every odd $r$, one of the two products $A_1$ and $A_1A_2$ is an s.m.p. and the other is an s.l.p. The conjecture concerns exact extremal products for the joint and lower spectral radii of this matrix family; the supplied source states it as unresolved.

record.title: Guo's lower-bound conjecture for Laplacian eigenvalues and degrees

record.title: Babai–Kantor–Lubotzky conjecture on expanders from finite simple groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a nonabelian finite simple group. A subset $S\subset G$ is **symmetric** when it is closed under taking inverses, and $\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$ denotes the Cayley graph of $G$ with generating set $S$. **Babai–Kantor–Lubotzky conjecture.** There are constants $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\lambda<1$ such that, for every nonabelian finite simple group $G$, there is a symmetric set $S\subset G$ of $2k$ generators for which

$$
\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)

record.title: Strong Wilf-equivalence is characterized by trivial equivalence for binary words
record.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be binary words. They are **strongly Wilf-equivalent** if $B_{n,p}(k)=B_{n,q}(k)$ for all $n,k\geq 0$, and they are **trivially equivalent** when they are related by the trivial equivalence defined earlier in the paper.

**Strong Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** Two binary words $p$ and $q$ are strongly Wilf-equivalent if and only if they are trivially equivalent.

Strong Wilf-equivalence refines ordinary Wilf-equivalence, since words of the same length are Wilf-equivalent. The paper notes that strong Wilf-equivalence forces $p$ and $q$ to have the same length and the same number of runs of each size, while computations suggest that trivial equivalence gives all such equivalences.

record.title: Polynomial-size uniform subset conjecture for transitive group actions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a group that acts transitively on a set $X$. A subset $T\subset G$ is **$X$-uniform** if, for every $x,y\in X$, 

$$
\frac{1}{|T|}|\{g\in T:g(x)=y\}|=\frac{1}{|X|}.
$$

**Polynomial-size uniform subset conjecture.** There exists an $X$-uniform subset $T\subset G$ such that

$$
|T|\le |X|^c
$$

for some universal constant $c>0$. This conjecture asks whether the isolation condition used in the paper's general existence theorem is redundant. It would imply polynomial-size designs for every transitive group action; the source identifies this as an open problem in design theory.

record.title: Real-root conjecture for fully packed loop polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a matching, let $A_\pi(t)$ be its polynomial, let $d(\pi)$ denote the relevant degree, and let $m_p(\pi)$ denote the multiplicity assigned to the integer $p$. **Real-root conjecture.** All real roots of $A_\pi(t)$ are negative integers, with $-p$ occurring with multiplicity $m_p(\pi)$; equivalently, 
$$
A_\pi(t)=\frac{1}{|d(\pi)|!}\left(\prod_{p=1}^{|\pi|-1}(t+p)^{m_p(\pi)}\right)Q_\pi(t),
$$
 where $Q_\pi(t)$ is an integer-coefficient polynomial with no real roots. The conjecture is supported by exact computations for all matchings of size at most $8$, but no general proof or disproof is given here.

317601.title: Johnson–Holroyd–Stahl conjecture on the circular chromatic number of Kneser graphs
317601.literal_statement:
Let ${\rm KG}(m,n)$ denote the Kneser graph, whose vertices are the $n$-element subsets of an $m$-element set, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding subsets are disjoint. Write $\chi(G)$ for the chromatic number and $\chi_c(G)$ for the circular chromatic number. **Johnson–Holroyd–Stahl conjecture.** For all $m\geq 2n+1$, 

$$
\chi_c({\rm KG}(m,n))=\chi({\rm KG}(m,n)).
$$

Equality of the two chromatic parameters is known in several cases, including $m\leq 2n+2$ or $n=2$, but the statement was presented as a conjecture for all Kneser graphs in the source.

374484.title: Rayleigh conjecture for spanning-forest generating functions
374484.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, and let $F_G(\mathbf{w})$ denote its spanning-forest generating function (SFGF), where $\mathbf{w}$ is the vector of edge weights. A multivariate polynomial is **Rayleigh** when it satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for all nonnegative edge weights.

**Spanning-forest Rayleigh conjecture.** For any graph $G=(V,E)$, the SFGF $F_G(\mathbf{w})$ is Rayleigh.

A positive answer would imply that the spanning-forest distribution on a graph is negatively correlated, connecting the claim to conjectures of Kahn and of Grimmett and Winkler. The source does not specify whether this conjecture has been resolved.

380353.title: The uniform partially-intersecting partition-system conjecture
380353.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}^n_k$ be the family of uniform $k$-partitions of an $n$-set. Two partitions are **partially $t$-intersecting** if some class from each has intersection of size at least $t$.

**Uniform partial-intersection conjecture.** Let $k,c,t$ be positive integers with $t\leq c$ and $n=ck$. If $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{U}^n_k$ is partially $t$-intersecting, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq\binom{n-t}{c-t}U(n-c,k-1).
$$
 Moreover, equality holds if and only if, up to a permutation of $[1,n]$, 
$$
\mathcal{P}=\{P\in\mathcal{U}^n_k:[1,t]\subseteq P_i\text{ for some }P_i\in P\}.
$$
 

The conjecture generalizes the preceding partially 2-intersecting problem from arbitrary partition systems to uniform partition systems.

379976.title: Avoidability threshold for powers in odd-difference arithmetic progressions
379976.literal_statement: Let an infinite word be a sequence over a 4-letter alphabet. An **$r$-power** is a word consisting of repetitions of a nonempty block with exponent $r$, and a word **avoids $r$-powers in arithmetic progressions of odd difference** if no such factor occurs along an arithmetic progression whose common difference is odd. **The power-avoidability conjecture.** For every real number $r<2$, $r$-powers are not avoidable in arithmetic progressions of odd difference over a 4-letter alphabet. The construction above gives uncountably many 4-letter words avoiding squares in arithmetic progressions of odd difference, but each such word contains $r$-powers for every $r<2$; a backtracking search confirms the conjecture for $r\leq 7/4$, while the general range $7/4<r<2$ remains open.

378964.title: Nonnegative symmetric decomposition conjecture for fixed-point-free involution Eulerian polynomials
378964.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}_{2n}$ be the set of fixed-point-free involutions in $\mathfrak{S}_{2n}$, and let $J_{2n,k}$ count those with $k$ descents. Define

$$
J_{2n}(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}J_{2n,k}t^k.
$$

Using the symmetric expansion

$$
J_{2n}(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}b_{2n,k}t^k(1+t)^{2n-2k},
$$

**Nonnegative decomposition conjecture.** For $n\geq 9$ and $k\geq 1$, the coefficients $b_{2n,k}$ are nonnegative integers.

The coefficients are given by explicit alternating sums and are shown to grow with $n$ for each fixed $k>1$, but the stated nonnegativity for all $n\geq 9$ and $k\geq 1$ remains unproved in the source.

379037.title: Babson–Kozlov vanishing conjecture for odd-cycle Hom-complexes
379037.literal_statement:
Let $C_{2r+1}$ be an odd cycle, let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\varpi_1^{n-2}(\text{\tt Hom}(C_{2r+1},K_n))$ denote the indicated Stiefel-Whitney characteristic class. **Babson–Kozlov vanishing conjecture.** For every positive integer $r$ and every $n\geq 2$, one has

$$
\varpi_1^{n-2}(\text{\tt Hom}(C_{2r+1},K_n))=0.
$$

The source records proofs for $r=1$ and for odd $n$, as well as the case $(r,n)=(2,4)$, but leaves the general claim unresolved.

379281.title: Lower bound for the number of distinct multinomial coefficients
379281.literal_statement:
Let $M(n)$ be the number of distinct multinomial coefficients arising from partitions of $n$, and let $p^*(n)$ be the total number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are either at most $6$ or multiples of $3$ (or both). **Lower-bound conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 0$,

$$
M(n)\geq p^*(n).
$$

This conjecture gives a combinatorial lower bound for the number of distinct multinomial coefficients and is part of the paper's proposed description of the growth of $M(n)$.

379445.title: The genericity conjecture for Bruhat-graph sheaf inclusions
379445.literal_statement:
Let $({\mathcal W},{\mathcal S})$ be a Coxeter system with length function $l$, and let ${\mathscr B}(x)^{[y]}\hookrightarrow {\mathscr B}(x)^y$ be the inclusion of the costalk into the stalk for $y<x$. For a graded module $M$, let $M_{\{\leqslant k\}}$ denote the submodule generated in degrees at most $k$. **The genericity conjecture.** For every $x,y\in{\mathcal W}$ with $y<x$, this inclusion is generic in the sense that, for every $m\geq 1$,

$$
{\mathscr B}(x)^{[y]}_{\{\leqslant l(x)-l(y)+m-1\}}\cap {\mathscr B}(x)^y_{\{\leqslant l(x)-l(y)-m\}}=0.
$$

The paper proves that this conjecture implies the degree conjecture, placing it in the proposed inductive route to the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

379446.title: The Hard Lefschetz decomposition conjecture for Bruhat-graph sheaves
379446.literal_statement:
Choose a generic line in $V^\ast$ and let $\rho:S\to{\mathbb R}[T]$ be the corresponding graded surjection, with $T$ of degree $2$. For an $S$-module $M$, set $M_T=M\otimes_S{\mathbb R}[T]$. Let ${\mathscr B}(x)^{\delta y}_T$ be the indicated quotient module associated with the stalk and costalk of ${\mathscr B}(x)$ at $y$. **The Hard Lefschetz decomposition conjecture.** For every $x,y\in{\mathcal W}$ with $y<x$, the ${\mathbb R}[T]$-module ${\mathscr B}(x)^{\delta y}_T$ is isomorphic to a direct sum of modules of the form

$$
\left({\mathbb R}[T]/T^{n+1}\right)\{-(l(x)-l(y))+n\},\qquad n\geq 0.
$$

This is the algebraic Hard Lefschetz-type statement used to imply the genericity conjecture, and hence the degree conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

379447.title: The Hard Lefschetz isomorphism conjecture for Bruhat-graph sheaves
379447.literal_statement:
Choose a generic line and the associated graded algebra ${\mathbb R}[T]$, with $T$ of degree $2$, and let ${\mathscr B}(x)^{\delta y}_T$ be the corresponding module. **The Hard Lefschetz property.** For $x,y\in{\mathcal W}$ with $y<x$, multiplication by $T^m$ induces an isomorphism

$$
T^{m}:{\mathscr B}(x)^{\delta y}_{T,\{l(x)-l(y)-m\}}\stackrel{\sim}{\longrightarrow}{\mathscr B}(x)^{\delta y}_{T,\{l(x)-l(y)+m\}}
$$

for every $m\geq 1$.
This is the second Hard Lefschetz formulation in the paper and is presented after the decomposition conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

378699.title: Stable matching existence under the circular rule
378699.literal_statement:
A 3G matching market has three categories of agents, such as women, men, and dogs. Under the **circular rule**, women care only about the man, men care only about the dog, and dogs care only about the woman they are matched with; a **stable matching** has no blocking coalition under this rule.

**Circular-rule existence conjecture.** Under the circular rule, every 3G matching market has a stable matching.

The circular rule is described as a special case of the strongest link rule. Computer experiments found many stable matchings in circular markets, but existence for arbitrary market sizes remains open.

377805.title: The conjectural formula for Kontsevich cycles $[W_{n,k}^\ast]$
377805.literal_statement:
Let $W_{n,k}^\ast$ be the Kontsevich cycle indexed by nonnegative integers $n$ and $k$, and let $\widetilde{\kappa}_j$ denote the corresponding modified kappa class. Write $(2m+1)!!$ for the odd double factorial. **The conjectural formula for $[W_{n,k}^\ast]$.** One should have

$$
[W_{n,k}^\ast]=(-2)^{n+k+2}(2n+1)!!(2k+1)!!(\widetilde{\kappa}_n\widetilde{\kappa}_k-\widetilde{\kappa}_{n+k})-(-2)^{n+k+1}(2n+2k+3)!!\widetilde{\kappa}_{n+k}.
$$

When $n=k$, the right-hand side should be divided by $2$. This conjecture extrapolates the formulas established for the cases $k=0$ and $k=1$ and predicts a symmetric expression for all Kontsevich cycles; its general validity is not established in the supplied text.

377899.title: Monotonicity of relaxation time for ferromagnetic Ising Glauber dynamics
377899.literal_statement: Let $G$ be any graph equipped with a ferromagnetic Ising model, with couplings $J_{xy}$, and let $\tau_2$ denote the relaxation time of its Glauber dynamics. **Peres's monotonicity conjecture.** For the ferromagnetic Ising model on any graph, the relaxation time $\tau_2$ is an increasing function of any of the couplings $J_{xy}$. This conjecture asks how the relaxation time depends on interaction strengths; the paper proves the corresponding monotonicity result when $G$ is a cycle, while the assertion for arbitrary graphs is left open in the source.

378065.title: Quantum nonnegative monomial-basis conjecture for crystallographic Coxeter systems
378065.literal_statement: Let $(W,S)$ be a crystallographic Coxeter system, let $qBE(W,S)$ be the associated quantum algebra, and let $\tilde{P}_w\in {\bf S}(V^{\ast})\otimes {\bf R}[q_s]$ be the polynomial characterized by $[\tilde{P}_w](1)=w$ and by its triangular expansion in the polynomials $X_v$. **Quantum nonnegative monomial-basis conjecture.** There exists a monomial basis $\{b_{\mu}\}_{\mu}$ of $qBE(W,S)$ such that, for every $w\in W$, the element $[\tilde{P}_w]$ is a linear combination of the basis elements $b_{\mu}$ with nonnegative coefficients that do not depend on the parameters $q_s$. This is the quantum analogue of the preceding positivity conjecture; the supplied passage gives no resolution status or further evidence.

377463.title: Finiteness conjecture for cyclically 4-connected cubic flow roots
377463.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cyclically 4-connected cubic graph, and let $F(G,t)$ denote its flow polynomial. Let $\tau=(1+\sqrt{5})/2$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many cyclically 4-connected cubic graphs have a flow root in

$$
(2,\tau^2-\epsilon).
$$

This is the flow-polynomial counterpart of the finiteness conjecture for 4-connected plane triangulations. The source presents it as open.

377663.title: The face-subgraph characterization conjecture for compact visibility graphs
377663.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. For each internal face $F$ in a plane drawing of $G$, let $G_F$ denote the subgraph induced by the vertices incident with $F$. **Compact visibility conjecture.** The graph $G$ is a compact visibility graph if and only if it has a plane drawing such that, for every internal face $F$, the graph $G_F$ is a compact visibility graph.

This would characterize compact visibility graphs through the compact visibility of the subgraphs induced by the boundaries of internal faces. The statement is motivated by the failure of the analogous characterization using only triangular internal faces, since $K_{1,1,n}$ is a compact visibility graph but has no plane drawing with all internal faces triangular for $n\geq 3$.

377197.title: Isoperimetric criterion for bounded percolation thresholds
377197.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph and define 

$$
\delta(G)=\sup\{\alpha:|\partial S|\geq |S|^\alpha\text{ for all }S\subset G,
\ |S|\leq |G|/2\}.
$$

Here $\partial S$ is the vertex boundary used in the paper, and $p^G$ is the percolation threshold. **Isoperimetric-threshold conjecture.** If $\delta(G)>\delta>0$, then there is a function $f$ such that $p^G<f(\delta)<1$. This is proposed as a sharpening of an earlier theorem and is left open.

377105.title: Stanley's reformulation of Kontsevich's polynomial-counting conjecture
377105.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph with edge set $E(G)$, and let

$$
Q_G=\sum_T\prod_{e\in T}x_e,
$$

where the sum runs over spanning trees $T$ of $G$. Let $V(Q_G)$ be the zero scheme of $Q_G$ in $\mathbf A^{E(G)}$, let $X_G=\mathbf A^{E(G)}\setminus V(Q_G)$, and write $[X_G](q)=\#X_G(\mathbf F_q)$. **Stanley's reformulation.** For all graphs $G$, $[X_G]$ is a polynomial in $q$. Stanley showed that this conjecture is equivalent to Kontsevich's conjecture for $Y_G$. The paper's main theorem disproves the equivalent Kontsevich conjecture, so this reformulation is refuted as well.

321516.title: Hansen–Johnsen–Ranestad conjecture on higher weights of Grassmann codes
321516.literal_statement: Let $G(l,m)$ be the Grassmann variety of $l$-dimensional subspaces of an $m$-dimensional vector space over ${\mathbb F}_q$, embedded in the Plücker projective space $\mathbf P^{k-1}$, where $k=\binom{m}{l}$. Let $d_i$ be the higher weights of the Grassmann code $C(l,m)$, and let $J_i$ be the maximal number of ${\mathbb F}_q$-rational points of $G(l,m)$ lying on a codimension $i$ linear subspace of the Plücker space. A **Schubert union** is a union of Schubert varieties in $G(l,m)$. **Hansen–Johnsen–Ranestad's conjecture.** The higher weights of the Grassmann codes $G(l,m)$ are always computed by Schubert unions: for every $i$, there is a codimension $i$ linear subspace whose intersection with $G(l,m)$ is a Schubert union containing $J_i$ ${\mathbb F}_q$-rational points, and hence $d_i=n-J_i$. The conjecture predicts that Schubert unions suffice to attain the maxima governing all higher weights; the paper's stated goal is to confirm it in the case $l=2$, while the general assertion is presented as the conjecture from the cited work.

321613.title: Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan collapse conjecture for semidirect products
321613.literal_statement:
Let $G\cong \mathbb{Z}/m$ be a finite cyclic group, let $L\cong\mathbb{Z}^n$ be a finitely generated free abelian group, let $\rho\colon G\to\operatorname{aut}_{\mathbb{Z}}(L)$ be a group homomorphism, and set $\Gamma=L\rtimes_{\rho}G$. The Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence associated to the semidirect product $L\rtimes_{\rho}G$ has terms arising from the extension $1\to L\to\Gamma\to G\to 1$. **Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan conjecture.** The spectral sequence collapses in the strongest sense: all differentials in the $E_r$-term for $r\geq 2$ are trivial and all extension problems at the $E_{\infty}$-level are trivial. In particular, for all $k\geq 0$, 

$$
H^k(\Gamma;\mathbb{Z})\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=k}H^i(G;H^j(L)).
$$

The paper proves the conjecture when the $G$-action on $L$ is free outside the origin, but gives an example with $n=6$ and $m=4$ in which the second differential does not vanish; thus the conjecture is false in general.

record.title: The $d$-step conjecture for simple polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $d$-polytope with $2d$ facets, and let $u$ and $v$ be two **complementary vertices**, meaning vertices not lying in a common facet. **The $d$-step conjecture.** There is a path of length $d$ from $u$ to $v$.

This is the crucial $n=2d$ case underlying the Hirsch and non-revisiting conjectures. Its status is not established by the supplied source context.

record.statement: **Conjecture 2.** For any embedding of a cubic graph in an orientable surface $S_g$ such that $\operatorname{ew}(G^*)\ge 3$, we have $\phi_c(G)=4$. Equivalently, every cubic graph embedded in $S_g$ with $\operatorname{fw}(G)\ge 3$ is three-edge-colourable. Here $\operatorname{fw}(G)$ is the least number of points in which a noncontractible curve in $S_g$ meets $G$, and, for cubic embedded graphs, $\operatorname{fw}(G)=\operatorname{ew}(G^*)$.

record.title: Narayana distribution conjecture for path lengths of 231-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $S_n(231)$ denote the set of $231$-avoiding permutations of $[n]$. For $\pi\in S_n(231)$, let $\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)$ be the length of the path corresponding to $\pi$ under the construction above, and let $N(n,k)$ be a Narayana number.

**Narayana distribution conjecture.** The path lengths have the Narayana distribution:

$$
\sum_{\pi \in S_n(231)} q^{\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)} = q^{2n} \sum_{k \ge 0} N(n,k)q^{2k}.
$$

Moreover,

$$
\sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{\pi \in S_n(231)}q^{\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)} = \frac{1-q^2+q^4-\sqrt{1-2q^2-q^4-2q^6+q^8}}{2q^4}.
$$

The conjecture identifies the length statistic arising from the bijective construction with the Narayana distribution and gives its bivariate generating function. The paper presents this as an observed pattern supported by computations; no proof or resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Karp's evasiveness conjecture for monotone graph properties
record.statement: Let a graph property be a partition of the unlabeled graphs on a fixed number of vertices into graphs with and without the property. The property is **monotone** if it is preserved under the removal of edges. Associate to it the simplicial complex whose vertices are graph edges and whose simplices are the graphs having the property. A simplicial complex is **nonevasive** if it is a point, or if it has a vertex whose link and deletion are both nonevasive; it is **evasive** if it is not nonevasive. **Karp's conjecture.** All nontrivial monotone graph properties are evasive. The conjecture concerns the decision-tree complexity of graph properties and has connections with combinatorial and algebraic topology. It was proved for a prime-power number of vertices and for $n=6$ by Kahn, Saks, and Sturtevant; the paper studies possible counterexamples for $n=10$.

record.title: Nonexistence of a finite planar fair-win goal set
record.statement: In the planar achievement game, a finite point set $G\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is used as the goal set: players alternately place points, and Player 1 seeks to build a congruent copy of $G$ before Player 2 does. A **fair win** is a win in which Player 1 builds a goal set on a turn preceding every turn on which Player 2 builds one. **Planar fair-win nonexistence conjecture.** There is no finite point set $G\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ for which Player 1 has a strategy ensuring a fair win in the $G$-achievement game played in the plane. The preceding examples show that fair wins can occur for finite hypergraphs, but the claim asserts that no finite planar point set has this property.

record.title: Characterization of extremal incomplete sets in cyclic groups of order $pq$
record.statement:
Let $p,q$ be two odd prime numbers and let $G=Z_{pq}$. Write ${\rm cr}(G)$ for the critical number of $G$, and call a subset **incomplete** when its subset sums do not cover $G$. Assume

$$
p<q\leq p+\lfloor2\sqrt{p-2}\rfloor+1,
$$

$|A|={\rm cr}(G)-1=p+q-2$, and $0\notin A$.

**Extremal-set conjecture.** There exists an element $g\in G$ of order $pq$ such that

$$
A=\{\pm g,\pm 2g,\ldots,\pm \frac{p+q-2}{2}g\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a classification of the extremal incomplete sets in the stated range. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

record.title: Maximal-coefficient conjecture for Stern polynomials
record.statement:
Let

$$
B_{n}(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{e(n)}a_{i,e(n)}x^{i}
$$

and define

$$
\mathcal{M}(n)=\operatorname{max}\{a_{i,e(n)}:\;i=1,2,\ldots,e(n)\}.
$$

Then the following equality holds:

$$
\operatorname{max}\{\mathcal{M}(m):\;m\in[2^{n-1},2^{n}]\}=\operatorname{max}\{C(n,0),C(n-1,1),\ldots,C(n-k,k)\},
$$

where $k$ is equal to $n/2$ if $n$ is even and $(n-1)/2$ if $n$ is odd.

This conjecture arose from investigations of the sequence of maximal coefficients of the Stern polynomial $B_n(t)$. The supplied context does not define the coefficient notation $a_{i,e(n)}$ or the quantities $C(n,j)$, so those definitions and the conjecture's current status should be checked against the source.

record.title: Pointed splitting subspace conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\alpha\in{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}$ satisfy

$$
{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}={\mathbb F}_q(\alpha),
$$

and let $x\in{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}^*$. An $m$-dimensional pointed $\alpha$-splitting subspace with base point $x$ is a pair $(W,x)$ where $W$ is an $m$-dimensional $\alpha$-splitting subspace and $x\in W$. **Pointed splitting subspace conjecture.** The number of $m$-dimensional pointed $\alpha$-splitting subspaces of ${\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}$ with base point $x$ is

$$
q^{m(m-1)(n-1)}.
$$

The source states that this conjecture implies the earlier splitting-subspace and fiber conjectures, and that it is trivial when $m=1$ or $n=1$; it remains open in general.

record.title: Gács et al.'s prescribed-range polynomial conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q=p^n$ elements, and let $M=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_q\}$ be a multiset of $\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfying

$$
a_1+\cdots+a_q=0.
$$

A polynomial has **range** $M$ if its values on $\mathbb{F}_q$, counted with multiplicity, form $M$.

**Gács et al.'s conjecture.** Let $k<\sqrt{p}$. If no polynomial with range $M$ has degree less than $q-k$, then $M$ contains an element of multiplicity at least $q-k$.

The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is false over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $p>9$ and $k=q-\ell-1\geq 3$, so the claim is refuted in the source paper.

record.title: Homotopy-equivalent topological representations detect isomorphisms of matroids
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite CW complex that is not contractible, and let $(M,l)$ and $(N,l')$ be $\rho$-immersed matroids such that

$$
{
\mathscr T}_X(M,l) \simeq {\mathscr T}_X(N,l').
$$

Suppose there exists a surjective weak map $\tau:M\to N$. **Topological representation isomorphism conjecture.** Then $\tau^{\#}$ is an isomorphism.

This conjecture proposes that, for a noncontractible base complex, homotopy equivalence of the associated topological representations forces the induced map on the relevant matroid data to be an isomorphism. The surrounding results establish strict Betti-number inequalities under rank-decreasing surjective weak maps, but the stated implication is not resolved here.

321501.title: Regularity conjecture for uniquely $K_r$-saturated graphs
321501.literal_statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. A graph is **uniquely $K_r$-saturated** if it is $K_r$-free and adding any missing edge creates exactly one copy of $K_r$; a **dominating vertex** is a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. A graph is **regular** if all its vertices have the same degree.

**Regularity conjecture.** For each $r$, a uniquely $K_r$-saturated graph with no dominating vertex is regular.

All examples known in the source are regular, which motivates this conjecture. Its resolution is not supplied and remains open in the paper's context.

321554.title: The maximal-dimension conjecture for 1-spec matrix spaces
321554.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a $1$-spec subspace of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ such that

$$
\dim V=1+\binom{n}{2}.
$$

Assume $n>4$. A linear subspace $W$ of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ has a **trivial spectrum** if no element of $W$ has a nonzero eigenvalue. **Maximal-dimension conjecture.** There exists a linear subspace $W$ of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ with a trivial spectrum such that

$$
V=\mathbb{K}I_n+W.
$$

The conjecture concerns the classification of $1$-spec subspaces of maximal dimension and, if true, would resolve the question for $\#\mathbb{K}>2$ and $n>4$ using the cited results on affine spaces of nonsingular matrices. Its status is not established in the supplied text.

321621.title: The extension-graph conjecture for right-angled Artin groups
321621.literal_statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be finite graphs. For a graph $\Gamma$, its **extension graph** $\Gamma^e$ has as vertices the elements of $A(\Gamma)$ conjugate to vertices of $\Gamma$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding elements commute. Write $\Lambda\leq\Gamma^e$ when $\Lambda$ is an induced subgraph of $\Gamma^e$.

**Extension-graph conjecture.**

$$
A(\Lambda)\leq A(\Gamma)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\Lambda\leq\Gamma^e.
$$

The forward implication is conjectured because every known embedding has arisen from an inclusion into an extension graph; the reverse implication is established by the paper's first main theorem. The conjecture remains unresolved in general, although it is proved when the target graph $\Gamma$ is triangle-free.

321728.title: Locating chromatic number of Kneser-type Cartesian products
321728.literal_statement:
Let $n\geq 3$ and define

$$
m_0=\max\{k\mid k\in\mathbb{N},\ k(k-1)-1\leq n\}.

321938.title: The two-dimensional sumset lower-bound conjecture for valid multisets
321938.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a **valid multiset** contained in $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$: it contains no zero element, and every nontrivial subgroup contains fewer than $p$ elements of $A$, counted with multiplicity. Write $|A|$ for the total multiplicity of $A$ and $\#\Sigma A$ for the number of distinct elements in its sumset. Assume

$$
p\leq |A|\leq 2p-3.
$$

**The two-dimensional sumset lower-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
\#\Sigma A\geq (|A|+2-p)p.
$$

Equivalently, if $|A|=p+k$ with $0\leq k\leq p-3$, then $\#\Sigma A\geq (k+2)p$. This conjecture seeks the sharp improvement of the one-dimensional lower bound for sumsets in $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$ under the validity restriction; it is the $m=2$, $q=1$ case of the wider conjecture stated later in the paper.
321938.actual_review_depth: All three source PDFs retrieved; latest Conjecture 1.6 and sharp example; journal version; Matomaki On sumsets of multisets in Z_p^m, Theorem 5 and full Section 3 proof read.
321938.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Matomaki Conjecture 4 is exactly the bound for size p+k, k<=p-3, plus an extra endpoint. Theorem 5 proves it for every k, using saturation of one-dimensional fibers, induction, and extension to size 2p-2. Therefore it directly includes the literal assigned statement.
321938.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Zero discovery credit. Auxiliary Lemmas 13–16 and publication chronology not completely independently audited; no new witness or alternative proof pursued.

322014.title: The strongly stratified and locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture
322014.literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated reflection group acting on a complex vector space $V$. A **frame** $\Lambda$ is the auxiliary structure used to define the properties strongly stratified and locally conical for the system $(W,R,\Lambda)$. **The strongly stratified and locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture.** For each well-generated reflection group $W$, there exists a generating set $R$ and a frame $\Lambda$ such that

$$
|R|=\dim V,
$$

$(W,R,\Lambda)$ is strongly stratified, and $(W,R,\Lambda)$ is locally conical. This is proposed as a partial extension of the paper's preceding results on stratification and conicality; the existence of such a generating set and frame is not established in the supplied text.

322024.literal_statement:

322081.title: The classification conjecture for APN power functions with exponent $2^t-1$
322081.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbb F}_{2^n}$ be the finite field with $2^n$ elements, and for $2\leq t\leq n-1$ define

$$
G_t:{\mathbb F}_{2^n}\to {\mathbb F}_{2^n},\qquad G_t(x)=x^{2^t-1}.
$$

A function is **APN** if its differential uniformity is at most $2$. **The classification conjecture.** If $G_t$ is APN, then either $t=2$, or $n$ is odd and

$$
t\in\left\{\frac{n+1}{2},n-1\right\}.
$$

The three listed cases are respectively the quadratic function $x\mapsto x^3$, the function with $t=(n+1)/2$ for odd $n$, and the inverse permutation with $t=n-1$ for odd $n$. The conjecture asks whether these are the only APN functions in this family; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
322081.actual_review_depth: Both versions Conjecture 1; source conclusion and named three families. A 2022 primary problem list identifies the even-n case as solved by Gologlu.
322081.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Normalizing a nonzero derivative increment reduces APN to fibers of D_t(X)=(X+1)^(2^t-1)+X^(2^t-1). A refutation needs an additional exponent whose every derivative fiber has size <=2, not one collision-free sample.
322081.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: No new exponent or uniform odd-n exclusion. Even-n result is known; Gologlu proof body and all later APN classification bodies remain unread.

322271.title: The cubic-graph cycle-length conjecture for powers of two
322271.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $l$ be the length of a cycle in $G$. **Cubic-graph cycle-length conjecture.** There exist a cycle length $l$ in $G$ and a positive integer $k$ such that

322351.title: Base-cobase graph diameter conjecture for block matroids
322351.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a block matroid of rank $n$, meaning that its ground set is the disjoint union of two bases. 322711.title: The two-Kuratowski-edge conjecture for simultaneous crossing-criticality
322711.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $e$ and $f$ be Kuratowski edges of $G$, meaning that each belongs to a subgraph homeomorphic to $K_{3,3}$ or $K_5$. 322716.title: Nonnegative coefficient conjecture for three-residue partition products
322716.literal_statement:
Let $L>0$, $z>1$, $y>z$, $y<x\leq y+z$, and $m\geq yz+2$. For the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q^m)_L=\prod_{j=0}^{L-1}(1-aq^{mj})$, define

$$
\frac{1}{(q,q^{x},q^{yz};q^{m})_L}-\frac{1}{(q^z,q^{y},q^{yz+1};q^{m})_L}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a(L,y,n,x,z,m)q^n.
$$

**Three-residue coefficient conjecture.** If $z$ does not divide $y$, then all coefficients $a(L,y,n,x,z,m)$ are non-negative; if $z$ divides $y$, then only finitely many of these coefficients are negative.

This conjecture extends the paper's partition inequalities to three residues and distinguishes the cases according to whether $z$ divides $y$. The authors state that it is motivated by experimental evidence and is being actively pursued; its resolution is not supplied here.

324369.title: Hansen's Szeged–Wiener index conjecture for bipartite graphs
324369.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected bipartite graph with $n \geq 4$ vertices and $m \geq n$ edges. Its Wiener index is

$$
W(G)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subseteq V(G)}d(u,v),
$$

and its Szeged index is

$$
Sz(G)=\sum_{e=uv\in E(G)}n_u(e)n_v(e),
$$

where $n_u(e)$ and $n_v(e)$ count the vertices closer to $u$ and $v$, respectively, for the edge $e=uv$. **Hansen's conjecture.**

$$
Sz(G)-W(G)\geq 4n-8.
$$

The bound is best possible: equality is attained by a graph formed from a $4$-cycle $C_4$ and a tree $T$ on $n-3$ vertices sharing one vertex. The conjecture concerns a lower bound relating two classical graph indices and, in the stated source, no resolution is supplied.

340762.title: Hamilton-circle conjecture from 2-connected radius-two balls
340762.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, infinite, locally finite graph. A **2-connected ball of radius $2$** is the subgraph induced by the vertices in such a ball that is 2-connected. For a path $uwv$ with $uv\notin E(G)$, let $d_G(u)$ and $d_G(v)$ denote the degrees of its endpoints, and let $M_2(w)$ denote the set of vertices at distance at most $2$ from $w$.

**Hamilton-circle conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a Hamilton circle if every ball of radius $2$ in $G$ is 2-connected and

$$
d_G(u)+d_G(v)\geq |M_2(w)|-1
$$

for each path $uwv$ with $uv\notin E(G)$.

This conjecture combines local 2-connectivity with a degree condition modeled on the finite Hamiltonicity criterion. The source explicitly says that the authors believe it is true but gives no proof or resolution, so it remains open.

340762.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need end-faithful connected limiting-cycle construction under the exact degree and radius-two hypotheses. A finite witness cannot by itself refute this infinite statement. Earlier three source families remain unread.

380376.title: Erdős et al.'s conjecture on avoiding triangles in two-colored planes
380376.literal_statement: Let $T$ be a triangle in the Euclidean plane, and let a **coloring** be a partition of $\mathbb{R}^2$ into two color classes. A coloring **contains** $T$ if it has a monochromatic copy of $T$ obtained by translations and rotations; otherwise, it **avoids** $T$. Let $\chi^*$ be the coloring by alternating half-open horizontal strips of width $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, with a point $(x,y)$ black if and only if $n\sqrt{3}<y\leq\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)\sqrt{3}$ for some integer $n$. **Erdős et al.'s conjecture.** For every triangle $T$ and every coloring $\chi$, if $\chi$ avoids $T$, then $T$ is an equilateral $(l,l,l)$-triangle and $\chi$ is equal to an $l$-times scaled copy of $\chi^*$, up to possible modifications of the colors of points on the boundary of the strips. The paper presents a counterexample to this conjecture and gives a broader class of colorings avoiding the unit triangle, so this conjecture is refuted.

381393.title: De Pierro's conjecture on underrelaxed projection limits
381393.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1,\ldots,C_N$ be nonempty closed convex subsets of $X$, with metric projections $P_{C_i}$. For $\lambda\in]0,1]$, define

$$
Q_{\lambda}:=((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_N})\cdots((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_2})((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_1}).
$$

Assume that $F_{\lambda}:=\operatorname*{Fix}Q_{\lambda}\neq\emptyset$ for every $\lambda\in]0,1]$. For $x\in X$, let

$$
x_{\lambda}=\operatorname*{weak}\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}Q_{\lambda}^{n}(x).
$$

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the set of least-squares solutions,

$$
\mathcal{L}:=\left\{x\in X\mid \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert x-P_{C_i}(x)\right\Vert^2=\inf_{y\in X}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert y-P_{C_i}(y)\right\Vert^2\right\}.
$$

**De Pierro's conjecture.** The weak limits satisfy

$$
\lim_{\lambda\rightarrow0^{+}}x_{\lambda}=P_{\mathcal{L}}(x).
$$

The conjecture concerns the behavior, as the underrelaxation parameter tends to zero, of weak limits generated by cyclic compositions of underrelaxed projections for inconsistent convex feasibility problems. It is false in general: a system of three compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ provides a counterexample.

primary_source.name: Yair Censor and Maroun Zaknoon, “Algorithms and Convergence Results of Projection Methods for Inconsistent Feasibility Problems: A Review”, arXiv:1802.07529 (2018).

379528.title: Hamiltonian cycle game's threshold conjecture
379528.literal_statement:

$$

$$

379845.title: Conjecture on diagonal-flip stabilization of surface triangulations
379845.literal_statement:
For a surface $S$, let $N(S)$ be the minimum value such that any two triangulations $T$ and $T'$ of $S$ with

$$
|V(T)|=|V(T')|\geq N(S)
$$

are equivalent under diagonal flips. Let $V_{\min}(S)$ be the minimum number of vertices in a triangulation of $S$.

**Conjecture on diagonal-flip stabilization.** The only surfaces $S$ for which

$$
N(S)=V_{\min}(S)
$$

are $S_0$, $S_1$, $S_2$, $N_1$, $N_2$, and $N_3$.

The equality means that flip-equivalence already holds at the minimum triangulation size. It is verified for the listed surfaces, while the paper gives counterexamples showing strict inequality for many higher-genus surfaces; the full exclusivity claim is left as a conjecture.

380616.title: Albertson–Grossman–Haas partial list coloring conjecture
380616.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with list-chromatic number $\chi_{\ell}$. For a positive integer $t\leq\chi_{\ell}$, assign each vertex a list of $t$ colors, and let $\lambda_t$ be the minimum, over all such list assignments, of the maximum number of vertices that can be properly colored from their lists. **Albertson–Grossman–Haas conjecture.** If $t\leq\chi_{\ell}$, then

$$
\lambda_t\geq\frac{tn}{\chi_{\ell}}.
$$

Equivalently, at least $tn/\chi_{\ell}$ vertices can be colored from every assignment of lists of size $t$. The conjecture is known in the cases $t=1$ and $t=\chi_{\ell}$, but remains open for $1<t<\chi_{\ell}$.

x_c=\left|\{i\mid c_i=c\}\right|,\qquad y_d=\left|\{i\mid d_i=d\}\right|.

record.title: The planar graph Markov width conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $mu(G)$ denote its Markov width.

**Planar graph Markov width conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C$ such that

$$
\mu(G) \leq C
$$

whenever $G$ is planar. Even more strongly, one may take $C=6$.

The conjecture is motivated by computations for small irreducible graphs and by the bounded-degree Markov bases known for cycles and complete bipartite graphs $K_{2,n}$.

record.title: The Zagreb index inequality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple connected graph with $n=|V|$ vertices and $m=|E|$ edges. Its first and second Zagreb indices are

$$
M_1=\sum_{i\in V}d_i^2,\qquad M_2=\sum_{(i,j)\in E}d_i d_j,
$$

where $d_i$ is the degree of vertex $i$. **Zagreb index inequality conjecture.** For all such graphs,

$$
\frac{M_1}{n}\leqslant\frac{M_2}{m},
$$

and the bound is tight for complete graphs. The conjecture was disproved for general connected graphs, but it was proven to hold for chemical graphs; this paper also identifies classes, such as subdivision graphs, for which it holds.
record.source_name: Aleksandar Ilić and Dragan Stevanović, “On comparing Zagreb indices”, arXiv:1104.4262 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.4262

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2011). “Nevertheless, it was proven in that the conjecture holds for chemical graphs.”

record.title: Finite cross-ratio conjecture for quaternionic unimodular matroids
record.statement:

record.title: Locating chromatic number bound for Cartesian products of connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, let $\square$ denote the Cartesian product, and write $\chi_L$ for the locating chromatic number. **Locating chromatic number bound for Cartesian products.** For every two connected graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$

record.title: The even-Wilf-equivalence refinement conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}_n(sigma)$ and $\mathcal{S}_n(sigma)$ denote, respectively, the even and unrestricted permutations in $\mathcal{S}_n$ avoiding $sigma$, and write $sigma equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} tau$ and $sigma equiv_{\mathcal{S}_n} tau$ for equality of the corresponding avoidance counts for every $n$. Then:

**Even-Wilf-equivalence refinement conjecture.** If

$$
sigma equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} tau,
$$

then

$$
sigma equiv_{\mathcal{S}_n} tau.
$$

Known equivalences and the conjectures in the paper suggest that even-Wilf-equivalence is a refinement of ordinary Wilf-equivalence.

record.title: Unique non-trivial fixed point on generalized spoke and star graphs
record.statement:
Consider a generalized spoke and star graph with $\ell$ levels. Level one consists of one node, the hub; level two consists of $n_1$ spokes connected to the hub; and each node at level $k$ has $n_k$ nodes connected to it at level $k+1$. **Unique-fixed-point conjecture.** The virus-dynamics system has a unique non-trivial fixed point if and only if

$$
b > \frac{1-a}{\sqrt{n_1+\cdots+n_{\ell-1}}}.
$$

The source notes that this is known for $\ell=2$ or $3$ and conjectures the general statement for arbitrary numbers of levels.

record.title: Balogh–Kostochka–Treglown degree-sequence conjecture for perfect clique packings
record.statement:
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r$ dividing $n$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices whose degree sequence is $d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_n$. **Balogh–Kostochka–Treglown conjecture.** If

$$
d_i\geq (r-2)n/r+i
$$

for every $i<n/r$, and

$$
d_{n/r+1}\geq (r-1)n/r,
$$

then $G$ contains a perfect $K_r$-packing. This degree-sequence condition is a sufficient-condition conjecture for perfect clique packings; the source does not specify whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Sum rules for the special values of fully packed loop polynomials
record.statement:
For a matching $\pi$, define $G_\pi=A_\pi(-|\pi|)$; let $A_n$ and $A_n^V$ denote the enumerative quantities used in the source, and let $^n$ denote the empty matching with $n$ nested arches. **Sum-rule conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, 
$$
\sum_{\pi:|\pi|=n}|G_\pi|=A_n,\qquad \sum_{\pi:|\pi|=n}G_\pi=(-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}(A_n^V)^2,

$$
G_{^n}=\begin{cases} (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}(A_{n+1}^V)^2,&n\text{ is even},\\ (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}A_n^VA_{n+2}^V,&n\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}
$$
 These identities describe striking global relations among the special values $G_\pi$; the source notes that part of the second equality follows from other conjectures, while the general conjectural picture remains open.

record.title: Power determinantal representation conjecture for real zero polynomials
record.statement:
Let $p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a **real zero polynomial** if, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{C}$, $p(\mu x)=0$ implies that $\mu$ is real. Suppose that $p(0)=1$. **Power determinantal representation conjecture.** There are symmetric matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ and a positive integer $N$ such that

$$
p(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^N=\det(I+x_1A_1+\cdots+x_nA_n).
$$

This is a relaxation of the Helton–Vinnikov conjecture, allowing a positive power of the polynomial. It is refuted in this paper using the nonrepresentability of the Vámos cube matroid, which has the half-plane property.

record.title: The word-polynomial local-solvability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $w$ be a finite word in the alphabet $\{X,A\}$, and let $P_w(x,y)\in\mathbb Z[x,y]$ be its word polynomial. A word is **totally decomposable** as defined by compositions of the maps $u\mapsto (uA^k)^m u$, $u\mapsto uA$, and $u\mapsto Au$.

**The word-polynomial local-solvability conjecture.** If $w$ is not totally decomposable, then the equation

$$
P_w(x^2,y^2)=0
$$

has a solution $(x_p,y_p)\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^*\times(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^*$ for all but finitely many primes $p$.

This condition, together with the paper's reduction theorem, would imply the totally decomposable word conjecture. The authors do not know whether the condition is sufficient, so the problem remains open.

record.title: The polynomial-denominator conjecture for generalized factor order
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}^*$ be the set of finite words over the positive integers, let $S(u;t,x)$ be the associated generating function, and let an **increasing/decreasing factorization** mean the factorization used in the paper. **Polynomial-denominator conjecture.** For every $u\in\mathbb{P}^*$,

$$
S(u;t,x)=\frac{x^s t^r}{P(u;t,x)},
$$

where $s$ and $r$ are integers and $P(u;t,x)$ is a polynomial, if and only if $u$ has an increasing/decreasing factorization. The claim is motivated by the limitations of the preceding technique and by experimental evidence; its general validity remains open.

record.title: The shifted-sum conjecture for pure O-sequences
record.statement:
Let $h=(1,h_1,\dotsc,h_e)$ and $h'=(1,h'_1,\dotsc,h'_{e-1})$ be pure $O$-sequences. For a vector $H=(1,H_1,H_2,\dots,H_t)$, write $\Delta H=(1,H_1-1,H_2-H_1,\dots,H_t-H_{t-1})$ for its first difference. Assume that $(\Delta h')_i\leq(\Delta h)_i$ for all $i\leq\lceil e/2\rceil$ and that $h'_i\leq h_i$ for all $i\leq e-1$. **Shifted-sum conjecture.** The shifted sum

$$
h”=(1,h_1+1,h_2+h'_1,\dotsc,h_e+h'_{e-1})
$$

is also a pure $O$-sequence. The conjecture is designed to support an inductive approach to Stanley's conjecture via deletion and links of matroid complexes, and is proved in the paper for small socle degrees.

record.title: Small-diameter obstruction for four pairs of points
record.statement:
Let $A_i=\{p_i,q_i\}$, $i=1,2,3,4$, be four sets of two points each in $\mathbf{R}^3$. For a set of points, call it **convexly independent** when every point is a vertex of its convex hull. **Small-diameter obstruction conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, whenever

$$
\lVert p_i-q_i\rVert_2<\varepsilon
$$

for every $i$, the set of midpoints between points in different $A_i$,

$$
\bigcup_{\substack{i,j=1,2,3,4,\\ i\neq j}}\frac12(A_i+A_j),
$$

is not convexly independent. This is presented as a sufficient condition for the preceding non-realizability conjecture, and concerns the local obstruction created by four pairs whose members are sufficiently close together.
record.source_name: Konrad J. Swanepoel and Pavel Valtr, “Large convexly independent subsets of Minkowski sums”, arXiv:1007.2775 (2010).

record.title: The Engel-word surjectivity conjecture for finite simple groups
record.statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the Engel words recursively by

$$
e_1(x,y)=[x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1},\qquad e_n(x,y)=[e_{n-1}(x,y),y]\quad(n>1).
$$

For a group $G$, let $e_n:G\times G\to G$ be the corresponding Engel word map.

**Engel-word surjectivity conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the map $e_n$ is surjective for every finite simple non-abelian group $G$.

The conjecture extends the question of whether nontrivial word maps are surjective on finite simple groups. The source records the commutator case as the Ore conjecture, which is solved, but does not establish the assertion for all Engel words and all finite simple groups.
record.source_name: Tatiana Bandman, Shelly Garion and Fritz Grunewald, “On the Surjectivity of Engel Words on PSL(2,q)”, arXiv:1008.1397 (2011).

record.title: The open amalgams conjecture for completely metrisable groups
record.statement:
A topological group $G$ is said to have **property (OA)** if, whenever $G=A*_CB$ is a non-trivial decomposition as a free product with amalgamation, the subgroups $A$, $B$, and $C$ are open in $G$. Here, non-trivial means that $A$ and $B$ are proper subgroups of $G$.

**Open amalgams conjecture.** Every completely metrisable topological group has property (OA).

Locally compact groups are known to have property (OA), and the paper proves the same for completely metrisable groups satisfying an additional somewhere-density condition. The conjecture proposes that this holds for all completely metrisable topological groups.

record.title: Subpolynomial vertex-stabiliser growth for almost simple tetravalent arc-transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let $c>0$. Let ${\mathcal F}_c$ be a finite family of graphs, let $G$ be an almost simple group, and let $\Gamma$ be a connected tetravalent $G$-arc-transitive graph with vertex $v$. **Vertex-stabiliser growth conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ is not contained in ${\mathcal F}_c$, then

$$
|G_v|<|\mathrm V\Gamma|^c.
$$

The graphs $\Delta_m$ provide examples in which the vertex-stabiliser grows faster than any logarithmic function of the number of vertices, but slower than every positive power. The conjecture asserts that, apart from finitely many exceptional graphs for each $c$, this subpolynomial bound holds for all connected tetravalent arc-transitive graphs with almost simple automorphism group.

record.title: Kajitani–Ueno–Miyano's Hamiltonian matroid conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be a matroid with rank function $r$. It is **Hamiltonian** if some cyclic ordering of $E$ has the property that every segment of $r(M)$ consecutive elements is a basis of $M$. It is **uniformly dense** if, for every nonempty subset $X\subseteq E$, 
$$
\frac{|X|}{r(X)}\leqslant\frac{|E|}{r(E)}.
$$
 **Kajitani–Ueno–Miyano's conjecture.** A matroid $M$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it is uniformly dense. Hamiltonian matroids are known to be uniformly dense, while the converse is stated as a conjecture and is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Marcin Anholcer, Maciej Bartkowiak, Bartłomiej Bosek and Jarosław Grytczuk, “Epistemic fair division of independence structures”, arXiv:2606.11494 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1011.1010](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.1010).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11494

record.title: The unique sum-point conjecture for complete arcs in $PG(2,q)$
record.statement:
Let $q$ be even, and let a **complete arc** in the projective plane $PG(2,q)$ mean an arc that cannot be enlarged by adding another point. Two arcs are **projectively equivalent** when a projectivity of $PG(2,q)$ maps one to the other; a **sum-point** is a point associated with the arc according to the paper's preceding definition. **Unique sum-point conjecture.** Every complete arc in $PG(2,q)$ is projectively equivalent to an arc with only one sum-point.

The conjecture proposes a canonical projective representative for every complete arc over an even-order field. Its status is not determined by the supplied text.

record.title: Sun's prime–Fibonacci-power representation conjectures
record.statement: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci sequence. A Fibonacci number is **positive** when its value is positive, and an odd Fibonacci number is one not divisible by $2$. **Sun's prime–Fibonacci-power conjectures.** (i) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, a positive Fibonacci number, and the square of a positive Fibonacci number; one of the two Fibonacci numbers can further be required to be odd. (ii) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, a positive Fibonacci number, and the cube of a positive Fibonacci number; one of the two Fibonacci numbers can further be required to be odd. The source reports computational verification for these assertions in substantial ranges, but gives no proof or disproof; they remain open.

record.title: Zhang's second conjecture on the lambda invariant of polarized metrized graphs
record.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a semistable fibration, let $CV(f)$ be the set of singular fibers, and let $\Gamma_y$ be the polarized metrized graph of the fiber over $y\in CV(f)$. For each node type $i$, let $\delta_i(\Gamma_y)$ denote its number. Let $\lambda(\Gamma)$ be Zhang's lambda invariant. **Zhang's second conjecture.** For every $y\in CV(f)$,

$$
\lambda(\Gamma_y)\geq\frac{\bar{g}}{8\bar{g}+4}\delta_0(\Gamma_y)+\sum_{i\geq1}\frac{i(\bar{g}-i)}{2\bar{g}+1}\delta_i(\Gamma_y).
$$

This inequality would yield a second proof of the stated slope inequality; the source gives no resolution status.

317926.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph and let $T\subseteq V(G)$. In the model $D_3^T(G)$, every edge is independently assigned one of its two orientations with equal probability. $$
P(u_\rightarrow\longrightarrow\mathrel{_{\rightarrow}v})\ge P(u_\rightarrow\longrightarrow\mathrel{_{\leftarrow}v}).

Write $(A_1,\ldots,A_k)\sim(B_1,\ldots,B_k)$ when the two tuples are equidistributed. **Refined joint equidistribution conjecture.**

$$
(T_1,T_2,T_3,S_{17})\sim(T_2,T_1,T_3,S_{17}).

This refinement is intended to preserve the statistic counting pairs that are simultaneously $S_{10}$ and $S_{12}$ while exchanging the two individual statistics; the source presents it as a likely consequence of the preceding conjecture.

318894.literal_statement:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. For variables $x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}$, let $\operatorname{CT}_{x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}}$ denote the constant term in their Laurent expansion. Then **the logarithmic odd Dyson conjecture.** Up to a sign,

$$
\operatorname{CT}_{x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}} \frac{1}{(x_1 \cdots x_{2k+1})^{(2m+1)k}} \prod_{i=1}^k \operatorname{ln}\left(1-\frac{x_{2i}}{x_{2i-1}}\right) \prod_{1 \leq i <j \leq 2k+1 }(x_i-x_j)^{2m+1}
$$

equals

$$
\frac{((2k+1)(2m+1))!!}{(2k+1)!!(2m+1)!!^{2k+1}}.
$$

This extends the preceding three-variable logarithmic constant-term identity in the direction of Dyson-type identities; the paper presents it as a precise conjecture, with no general proof supplied.
318894.ordinary_detail: Formal logarithm expands as minus sum z^r/r; the Laurent polynomial makes its relevant coefficient extraction finite, but multilog products require controlling simultaneous exponents and the double-factorial normalization. Differentiating a conjectural complex Dyson identity is conditional, not a proof. Specifically identified Chappell-Lascoux-Warnaar-Zudilin Logarithmic and Complex Constant Term Identities body unread; no claim it proves arbitrary k,m.

319338.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $f$ be compactly supported. A set $S$ is a **non-uniqueness set** for compactly supported functions $f$ if the corresponding acquisition data do not uniquely determine $f$. Let $\Sigma$ be the cone of zeros of a homogeneous harmonic polynomial, homogeneous with respect to some point in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $\Phi$ be an algebraic subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension at most $n-2$. **The higher-dimensional non-uniqueness-set conjecture.** The set $S$ is a non-uniqueness set for compactly supported functions $f$ if and only if

$$
S\subseteq\Sigma\cup\Phi.
$$

This conjectures the $n$-dimensional analogue of the known planar characterization of non-uniqueness sets, where, up to finitely many points, the set is a Coxeter cross. The result is stated as unproved in the source; only partial advances toward the higher-dimensional case are known.

2. If two groves intersect, their union is a grove.
3. Two maximal groves do not intersect.

record.title: The planar graph Markov width conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $mu(G)$ denote its Markov width.

**Planar graph Markov width conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C$ such that

$$
\mu(G) \leq C
$$

whenever $G$ is planar. Even more strongly, one may take $C=6$.

The conjecture is motivated by computations for small irreducible graphs and by the bounded-degree Markov bases known for cycles and complete bipartite graphs $K_{2,n}$.

record.title: The Zagreb index inequality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple connected graph with $n=|V|$ vertices and $m=|E|$ edges. Its first and second Zagreb indices are

$$
M_1=\sum_{i\in V}d_i^2,\qquad M_2=\sum_{(i,j)\in E}d_i d_j,
$$

where $d_i$ is the degree of vertex $i$. **Zagreb index inequality conjecture.** For all such graphs,

$$
\frac{M_1}{n}\leqslant\frac{M_2}{m},
$$

and the bound is tight for complete graphs. The conjecture was disproved for general connected graphs, but it was proven to hold for chemical graphs; this paper also identifies classes, such as subdivision graphs, for which it holds.
record.source_name: Aleksandar Ilić and Dragan Stevanović, “On comparing Zagreb indices”, arXiv:1104.4262 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.4262

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2011). “Nevertheless, it was proven in that the conjecture holds for chemical graphs.”

record.title: Finite cross-ratio conjecture for quaternionic unimodular matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ be the quaternions, with norm $|\cdot|$, and let $p,q,r\in\mathbb{H}$ satisfy

$$
|i-j|=1
$$

for all distinct $i,j\in\{0,1,p,q,r\}$. Let $M$ be a **quaternionic unimodular matroid (QU matroid)**, and let $(\mathbb{H},\langle-1,p,q,r\rangle)$ be the skew partial field generated by these elements. **Finite cross-ratio conjecture.** The matroid $M$ is representable over the skew partial field $(\mathbb{H},\langle-1,p,q,r\rangle)$. This is presented as a concrete conjectural restriction on the cross ratios needed for representations of QU matroids.

record.title: Locating chromatic number bound for Cartesian products of connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, let $\square$ denote the Cartesian product, and write $\chi_L$ for the locating chromatic number. **Locating chromatic number bound for Cartesian products.** For every two connected graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\chi_L(G\square H)\leq \max\{\chi_L(G),\chi_L(H)\}+3.
$$

The conjecture is suggested by the observation that graphs with larger diameter appear to have smaller locating chromatic number; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: The even-Wilf-equivalence refinement conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}_n(sigma)$ and $\mathcal{S}_n(sigma)$ denote, respectively, the even and unrestricted permutations in $\mathcal{S}_n$ avoiding $sigma$, and write $sigma equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} tau$ and $sigma equiv_{\mathcal{S}_n} tau$ for equality of the corresponding avoidance counts for every $n$. Then:

**Even-Wilf-equivalence refinement conjecture.** If

$$
sigma equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} tau,
$$

then

$$
sigma equiv_{\mathcal{S}_n} tau.
$$

Known equivalences and the conjectures in the paper suggest that even-Wilf-equivalence is a refinement of ordinary Wilf-equivalence.

record.statement:
Consider a generalized spoke and star graph with $\ell$ levels. Level one consists of one node, the hub; level two consists of $n_1$ spokes connected to the hub; and each node at level $k$ has $n_k$ nodes connected to it at level $k+1$. **Unique-fixed-point conjecture.** The virus-dynamics system has a unique non-trivial fixed point if and only if

$$
b > \frac{1-a}{\sqrt{n_1+\cdots+n_{\ell-1}}}.
$$

The source notes that this is known for $\ell=2$ or $3$ and conjectures the general statement for arbitrary numbers of levels.

record.title: Balogh–Kostochka–Treglown degree-sequence conjecture for perfect clique packings
record.statement:
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r$ dividing $n$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices whose degree sequence is $d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_n$. **Balogh–Kostochka–Treglown conjecture.** If

$$
d_i\geq (r-2)n/r+i
$$

for every $i<n/r$, and

$$
d_{n/r+1}\geq (r-1)n/r,
$$

then $G$ contains a perfect $K_r$-packing. This degree-sequence condition is a sufficient-condition conjecture for perfect clique packings; the source does not specify whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Sum rules for the special values of fully packed loop polynomials
record.statement:
For a matching $\pi$, define $G_\pi=A_\pi(-|\pi|)$; let $A_n$ and $A_n^V$ denote the enumerative quantities used in the source, and let $^n$ denote the empty matching with $n$ nested arches. **Sum-rule conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, 
$$
\sum_{\pi:|\pi|=n}|G_\pi|=A_n,\qquad \sum_{\pi:|\pi|=n}G_\pi=(-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}(A_n^V)^2,

$$
G_{^n}=\begin{cases} (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}(A_{n+1}^V)^2,&n\text{ is even},\\ (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}A_n^VA_{n+2}^V,&n\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}
$$

record.title: Power determinantal representation conjecture for real zero polynomials
record.statement:
Let $p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a **real zero polynomial** if, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{C}$, $p(\mu x)=0$ implies that $\mu$ is real. Suppose that $p(0)=1$. **Power determinantal representation conjecture.** There are symmetric matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ and a positive integer $N$ such that

$$
p(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^N=\det(I+x_1A_1+\cdots+x_nA_n).
$$

This is a relaxation of the Helton–Vinnikov conjecture, allowing a positive power of the polynomial. It is refuted in this paper using the nonrepresentability of the Vámos cube matroid, which has the half-plane property.
record.source_name: Petter Brändén, “Obstructions to determinantal representability”, arXiv:1004.1382 (2010).

record.title: The word-polynomial local-solvability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $w$ be a finite word in the alphabet $\{X,A\}$, and let $P_w(x,y)\in\mathbb Z[x,y]$ be its word polynomial. A word is **totally decomposable** as defined by compositions of the maps $u\mapsto (uA^k)^m u$, $u\mapsto uA$, and $u\mapsto Au$.

**The word-polynomial local-solvability conjecture.** If $w$ is not totally decomposable, then the equation

$$
P_w(x^2,y^2)=0
$$

has a solution $(x_p,y_p)\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^*\times(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^*$ for all but finitely many primes $p$.

This condition, together with the paper's reduction theorem, would imply the totally decomposable word conjecture. The authors do not know whether the condition is sufficient, so the problem remains open.

record.title: The polynomial-denominator conjecture for generalized factor order
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}^*$ be the set of finite words over the positive integers, let $S(u;t,x)$ be the associated generating function, and let an **increasing/decreasing factorization** mean the factorization used in the paper. **Polynomial-denominator conjecture.** For every $u\in\mathbb{P}^*$,

$$
S(u;t,x)=\frac{x^s t^r}{P(u;t,x)},
$$

where $s$ and $r$ are integers and $P(u;t,x)$ is a polynomial, if and only if $u$ has an increasing/decreasing factorization. The claim is motivated by the limitations of the preceding technique and by experimental evidence; its general validity remains open.

record.title: The shifted-sum conjecture for pure O-sequences
record.statement:
Let $h=(1,h_1,\dotsc,h_e)$ and $h'=(1,h'_1,\dotsc,h'_{e-1})$ be pure $O$-sequences. For a vector $H=(1,H_1,H_2,\dots,H_t)$, write $\Delta H=(1,H_1-1,H_2-H_1,\dots,H_t-H_{t-1})$ for its first difference. Assume that $(\Delta h')_i\leq(\Delta h)_i$ for all $i\leq\lceil e/2\rceil$ and that $h'_i\leq h_i$ for all $i\leq e-1$. **Shifted-sum conjecture.** The shifted sum

$$
h”=(1,h_1+1,h_2+h'_1,\dotsc,h_e+h'_{e-1})
$$

is also a pure $O$-sequence. The conjecture is designed to support an inductive approach to Stanley's conjecture via deletion and links of matroid complexes, and is proved in the paper for small socle degrees.

record.title: Small-diameter obstruction for four pairs of points
record.statement:
Let $A_i=\{p_i,q_i\}$, $i=1,2,3,4$, be four sets of two points each in $\mathbf{R}^3$. For a set of points, call it **convexly independent** when every point is a vertex of its convex hull. **Small-diameter obstruction conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, whenever

$$
\lVert p_i-q_i\rVert_2<\varepsilon
$$

for every $i$, the set of midpoints between points in different $A_i$,

$$
\bigcup_{\substack{i,j=1,2,3,4,\\ i\neq j}}\frac12(A_i+A_j),
$$

is not convexly independent. This is presented as a sufficient condition for the preceding non-realizability conjecture, and concerns the local obstruction created by four pairs whose members are sufficiently close together.

record.title: The Engel-word surjectivity conjecture for finite simple groups
record.statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the Engel words recursively by

$$
e_1(x,y)=[x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1},\qquad e_n(x,y)=[e_{n-1}(x,y),y]\quad(n>1).
$$

For a group $G$, let $e_n:G\times G\to G$ be the corresponding Engel word map.

**Engel-word surjectivity conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the map $e_n$ is surjective for every finite simple non-abelian group $G$.

The conjecture extends the question of whether nontrivial word maps are surjective on finite simple groups. The source records the commutator case as the Ore conjecture, which is solved, but does not establish the assertion for all Engel words and all finite simple groups.
record.source_name: Tatiana Bandman, Shelly Garion and Fritz Grunewald, “On the Surjectivity of Engel Words on PSL(2,q)”, arXiv:1008.1397 (2011).

record.title: The open amalgams conjecture for completely metrisable groups
record.statement:
A topological group $G$ is said to have **property (OA)** if, whenever $G=A*_CB$ is a non-trivial decomposition as a free product with amalgamation, the subgroups $A$, $B$, and $C$ are open in $G$. Here, non-trivial means that $A$ and $B$ are proper subgroups of $G$.

**Open amalgams conjecture.** Every completely metrisable topological group has property (OA).

Locally compact groups are known to have property (OA), and the paper proves the same for completely metrisable groups satisfying an additional somewhere-density condition. The conjecture proposes that this holds for all completely metrisable topological groups.
